newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to sell shares in mortgage bank-official.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to sell shares in mortgage bank-official.

text.p: The Argentine government said Thursday it will sell shares of state mortgage bank Banco Hipotecario, whose value has been estimated at between $3.0 to $3.5 billion.

Economy Minister Roque Fernandez, Cabinet Chief Jorge Rodriguez and Banco Hipotecario Chairman Pablo Rojo made the announcement at the end of a cabinet meeting, the state-run Telam new agency reported.
It was not immediately clear how many of the bank's shares would be sold. Local media had speculated that the Hipotecario would be sold off completely.
The private DyN new agency quoted Fernandez and Rojo as saying 90 percent of the shares would be sold.
It also quoted Fernandez as saying a $3.0 billion fund for public works and infrastructure would be set up with the proceeds from the stock sale.

The state will retain five percent of the Hipotecario shares and the bank will continue operating as a lending agency for house building. The fate of the remaining five percent was not immediately clear.
Rojo said no employees would be laid off or branches closed as a result of the sale. "The institution has been (financially) cleaned up and it is profitable," he said.
"The bank will retain special powers over outstanding loans and there will be no distortions in the financial system," Rojo added.
It was not immediately clear when the shares would be offered for sale, but Rojo was planning to hold a news conference at 1530 local (1830 GMT) to provide further details. -- David Haskel,
